absent: Full layouts of cred, inode, task_struct, task_delay_info, taskstats, syscall dispatch and signal action structures.
Security hook semantics for kernel act-as and create-files-as decisions.
Numeric values for capabilities, error codes, signal numbers, prctl modes, selector codes, DMA limits and address sentinel.
Slab cache flag effects and allocation context requirements beyond panic and account.
DMA lock protection scope and channel reservation rationale.
Memory parsing rules and core header consumption after boot.
Thread flag and syscall work bit assignments and architecture signal work.
Scheduler, probe, live-patch, futex, tick, RCU, lockdep and tracer internals referenced on return and interrupt paths.
Syscall number and argument retrieval, rollback mechanics and return trampoline detection.
Signal wakeup conditions and pending-state evaluation beyond forced delivery.

findings.text: Credential security override applies a caller-supplied security identifier to a proposed credential through the platform security hook and returns the hook decision unchanged.
File creation credential setup rejects unusable inode ownership, otherwise adopts the inode owner and group as filesystem identities in the proposed credential before requesting security approval.
Accumulated delay and processor-time totals reset to zero when unsigned addition would wrap, and a zero total combined with a nonzero count signals overflow rather than idleness.
Per-task delay state maintains separate total, count, extreme values and maximum timestamp for each stall category together with transient start marks and a dedicated synchronization object.
All mutations and snapshots of delay counters execute under the owning record lock with interrupt state preserved, covering completion, direct accumulation and statistics gathering paths.
Delay accounting startup creates a dedicated cache for per-task records, prepares the initial task entry and enforces the current global enablement selection.
Global enablement keeps a runtime branch and a plain flag consistent, supports boot-time activation, and permits runtime changes only through a privileged control with unprivileged writes denied.
Delay accounting control appears as task_delayacct under kernel with readable administrative permissions and accepts only disabled or enabled values.
Per-task delay preparation attempts a zeroed allocation from the dedicated cache and initializes the record lock only when allocation succeeds.
Statistics aggregation folds processor times, scheduler wait experience and every delay category from a target task into a cumulative record that preserves earlier contributions.
Scheduler wait fields are captured by single unsynchronized copies, deliberately tolerating inconsistency to avoid synchronization cost.
Delay start and completion paths assume a valid per-task record and do not test for absence, while only the aggregation path safely handles tasks lacking a record.
Reclaim stall tracking uses a per-task inside indicator plus caller-saved prior state so nested entries do not open new intervals and only the outermost exit closes the measurement.
Interrupt delay accounting adds a caller-provided delta directly to totals and event counts while maintaining extremes and maximum timestamp under protection.
Legacy DMA ownership uses a channel-indexed table where each slot holds a busy marker and an owner name, with one slot pre-reserved for cascade chaining.
Channel claim validates range, atomically acquires only idle entries and reports contention, while release warns on invalid or duplicate free without corrupting neighboring entries.
Configurations without DMA support expose a claim operation that always fails validation, a release with no observable effect, and a status view indicating unavailability.
DMA status initialization publishes a proc entry that lists busy channels with owner names when DMA support is present.
Core header location defaults to a maximum sentinel with zero size; its boot option accepts a single address or a size plus address pair and rejects missing or unparsable values.
User-return signal handling provides a weak no-effect default that architectures may replace with pending-work processing.
The user-return work loop exists in two build forms differing only in whether restartable-sequence work is handled inside the main loop or deferred to a separate restart stage.

User-return processing services scheduling, tracing, patching, signals, notifications and architecture work with interrupts allowed, then quiesces interrupts, refreshes flags and repeats until idle, with an outer check for sequence restarts.
Interrupt entry distinguishes user-mode from kernel-mode interruption and forwards to the matching entry path while returning state for exit handling.
Interrupt-exit rescheduling requires an enabled preemption context, a pending reschedule request and architecture consent, preceded by runtime and stack validation.
Conditional rescheduling on exit is further gated by a static branch that can suppress the entire check without altering call sites.
Interrupt exit selects user or kernel completion from the interrupted context, and nonmaskable transitions preserve disable tracking while bracketing tracing and instrumentation.
System call observation reports entry with call identity and exit with result, and audit capture records the call identity plus leading arguments for the audit path.
Dispatch violations raise SIGSYS with code SYS_USER_DISPATCH and carry the faulting address, execution architecture and attempted call number with zero error detail.

User dispatch filtering allows in-window origins and distinguished return paths, interprets an optional selector as allow, block or fatal misconfiguration with distinct terminal signals for access failure and bad values, otherwise records dispatch entry, rewinds the call and signals.
Forced signal handling holds the target signal-hand lock with interrupts saved across disposition review, default restoration, mask repair, protection-flag updates and queuing.

Forced delivery resets ignored, blocked or externally forced dispositions to default, marks terminal forced dispositions immutable, clears unkillable protection except for traced nonterminal victims, and ensures wakeup when no signal remains pending.

Dispatch configuration validates disable, exclusive and inclusive selections against overflow and empty ranges, inverts inclusive windows for the fast check, enforces a global arming gate, validates selector accessibility and installs window plus work-flag state.
Tracer access to dispatch state requires an exact-sized buffer and exchanges mode derived from the work flag together with window bounds and selector address, with user-copy faults reported.
Dispatch arming is governed by a kernel boolean defaulting to allowed with readable administrative permissions; denial blocks arming while still permitting disarming.
Completion timing discards nonpositive elapsed measurements, so clock nonmonotonicity or invalid start marks silently drop samples.
A DMA spin lock object is defined in these fragments without any shown acquisition scope, so its protection relationship cannot be established here.
Delay extremes treat an unset minimum as zero so the first positive sample establishes it, and maxima advance only when exceeded together with a fresh wall-clock stamp.
